title: C# 12, 13 and 14
cards/0/body: Constructor parameters go right in the class header. Key point: these are not properties but parameters available throughout the class body.
cards/1/q: Given class Service(IRepo repo), can outside code write service.repo?
cards/1/options/0: No: repo is a parameter, not a public property
cards/1/explain: In a record, positional parameters become properties; in a regular class they don't.
cards/2/body: Square brackets create an array, a list, a Span — whatever the target type needs. .. spreads another collection in.
cards/3/q: A list of zero, the elements of a, and five
cards/4/body:
params collections: params ReadOnlySpan<int> instead of an array — no allocation.
A new lock type, System.Threading.Lock (.NET 9): lock on it is faster than on an object.
ref struct in async methods — between awaits.
cards/5/body:
field — the hidden backing field of an auto-property.
extension blocks — extension properties, not just methods.
?.= — assign only if the left side is not null.
Implicit Span conversions: an array turns into a Span by itself wherever one is expected.
cards/6/q: Match the feature to the version
cards/7/q: What does order?.Status = Status.Paid do if order == null?
cards/8/q: What arrived in C# 12–14? Select all.
cards/8/explain: async is from C# 5, LINQ from C# 3.
